problems.stem: A particle moves at constant speed v = 20 m/s along a circular path of radius ρ = 50 m. What is its acceleration?
options: a = v²/ρ = 400/50 = 8 m/s² directed toward the center of curvature. Speed constant ⇒ a_t = 0; direction changing on a curve ⇒ a_n ≠ 0.
a = v/ρ = 0.4 m/s² in the tangential direction.
problems.explanation: Constant speed means tangential acceleration is zero. Normal (centripetal) acceleration is v²/ρ and always points to the center of curvature.

problems.stem: When are n-t coordinates the right choice over polar?
options: Always; n-t works in every case.
When the path is known and the question is about position along the path. For motion measured by distance and angle from a fixed origin, polar is usually simpler.
problems.explanation: Match the coordinate system to the geometry. n-t for path-defined motion; polar for origin-anchored motion.

problems.stem: In polar coordinates, why does the radial acceleration include a -rθ̇² term even when r̈ = 0?
options: It does not; if r̈ = 0 the radial acceleration is zero.
Because the unit vectors û_r and û_θ rotate as the particle moves; differentiating the rotating unit vectors generates additional terms. -rθ̇² is the centripetal-like contribution from this rotation.
problems.explanation: Rotating basis vectors are the source of polar-coordinate cross terms. They are not optional.

problems.stem: On a curved path, in which direction does the normal unit vector û_n point?
options: Toward the center of curvature of the path (always toward the inside of the turn). This is the same direction the centripetal acceleration acts.
Away from the center of curvature.
problems.explanation: û_n points toward the center of curvature. On a circular path, this is radially inward. Mistakenly pointing û_n outward flips the sign of the centripetal force equation.

problems.statement: A car rounds a curve of radius rho = 120 m. At the instant of interest its speed is v = 18 m/s and it is speeding up along the path at a_t = 2 m/s^2. Compute the magnitude of the total acceleration.
problems.hint: Find a_n = v^2/rho, then combine with the perpendicular a_t: |a| = sqrt(a_t^2 + a_n^2).
